skill.name: polish
skill.description: Final quality pass before shipping. Fixes alignment, spacing, consistency, and detail issues that separate good from great.
skill.summary: Review UI and product work for final polish before release.
skill.author: pbakaus

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and design terms such as grid and responsiveness. I found no evidence of command execution, system reconnaissance, network reconnaissance, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - **Type safety**: No TypeScript `any` or ignored errors
- **Pixel-perfect alignment**: Everything lines up to grid
- **Grid adherence**: Elements snap to baseline grid
- Enable grid overlay and verify alignment

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 94 uses Markdown inline code around prefers-reduced-motion in accessibility guidance. It is documentation text, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 154 uses Markdown inline code around the TypeScript any type. It does not execute a command or interpolate user-controlled input.
Line 41 refers to visual alignment on a design grid. This is UI layout guidance, not host or system reconnaissance.
Line 45 describes adherence to a baseline grid for interface layout. It does not collect system information or inspect the execution environment.
Line 48 asks the user to enable a visual grid overlay for alignment review. This is a browser or design inspection action, not system reconnaissance.
Lines 132-134 are a responsiveness checklist for breakpoints and touch targets. They do not instruct network scanning, probing, or external communication.

content.value_statement: Small interface issues can make complete work feel unfinished. This skill guides a final pass across visual detail, interaction states, accessibility, responsiveness, and code cleanliness.
actual_capabilities: Checklist-based review of visual alignment, spacing, typography, color, icons, forms, and copy.
Guidance for checking hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, and success states.
Accessibility reminders for contrast, keyboard navigation, focus indicators, labels, alt text, and touch targets.
Responsive quality checks across mobile, tablet, desktop, and supported browsers.
Code cleanup prompts for console logs, unused imports, type safety, and semantic HTML.
limitations: It does not replace automated tests, accessibility audits, or performance tooling.
It cannot verify real devices unless the agent has access to them.
It depends on project context, design tokens, and supported browser requirements.
It focuses on final quality, not early product strategy or feature design.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature for Release
use_cases.description: Run a structured final pass before shipping a completed interface.

use_cases.title: Check Implementation Fidelity
use_cases.description: Compare the built experience with intended spacing, typography, states, and responsive behavior.

use_cases.title: Triage Final Quality Work
use_cases.description: Identify the most visible polish issues when release time is limited.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Polish Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a completed page or feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the polish skill on the current feature. Focus on visible spacing, alignment, copy, and obvious interaction issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check Responsive and Accessible Details
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before a cross-device release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the polish skill to review mobile, tablet, and desktop behavior. Include contrast, focus states, labels, alt text, and touch targets.

prompt_templates.title: Review States and Edge Cases
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a workflow with async behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the polish skill to inspect loading, empty, error, disabled, success, hover, focus, and active states for this workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Release Polish
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced triage when release time is limited.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the polish skill to create a prioritized release polish pass. Separate blocking issues, high-impact refinements, and optional improvements.

output_examples.input: Polish the settings page before release.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering spacing inconsistencies, missing focus states, unclear labels, mobile layout issues, and final cleanup tasks.

output_examples.input: Check the checkout flow for final quality.
output_examples.output: A release-ready checklist with interaction states, error handling, loading feedback, accessibility concerns, and responsive issues to verify.

output_examples.input: Review this dashboard for polish gaps.
output_examples.output: A concise quality pass covering table density, chart labels, empty states, keyboard navigation, visual hierarchy, and copy consistency.

best_practices: Use it after core functionality is complete and before final release review.
Test the same workflow across supported viewports, themes, and interaction states.
Prioritize issues by user impact, release risk, and time available.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to polish unfinished features with unresolved product behavior.
Do not apply visual changes without retesting the affected workflow.
Do not perfect one small area while leaving broad consistency issues unresolved.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews visual polish, interaction states, accessibility basics, responsiveness, copy, performance signals, and code cleanliness.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after a feature works and before release, design review, or stakeholder approval.

faq.question: Can it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It highlights accessibility checks, but dedicated tools and manual testing are still required.

faq.question: Does it make design decisions?
faq.answer: It helps refine implementation details. It should follow your existing design system and product goals.

faq.question: Can it review code quality too?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes cleanup checks for console logs, unused imports, type safety, ARIA, and semantic HTML.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
